content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

Create an corner with two 140x140 plates at a 90° angle to each other. The first plate has in its center a cutout of 45x45. All plates are 10mm thick | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Implementation concept ‒ step by step (functions only)

1. Create the first plate  
   • Use functions.block with one solid block (subtraction = False).  
   • Dimensions: x-size = 140 mm, y-size = 140 mm, z-size = 10 mm (thickness).  
   • Base-point: (x,y,z) = (0, 0, 0).  
   → This produces a horizontal square plate lying in the XY-plane and 10 mm thick in +Z.

2. Cut the central opening in the first plate  
   • Use the same functions.block call, but as a second array entry with subtraction = True.  
   • Cut-out dimensions: 45 mm × 45 mm × 10 mm (full thickness).  
   • Its base-point must be centred:  
     – Plate’s mid-point is (70, 70).  
     – Half of 45 mm is 22.5 mm.  
     – Base-point = (70 – 22.5, 70 – 22.5, 0) = (47.5, 47.5, 0).  
   → This removes a 45 × 45 hole through the entire plate.

3. Add the second plate at 90°  
   • Add a third array entry to the same functions.block call (subtraction = False).  
   • This plate is vertical, lying in the YZ-plane; its thickness is 10 mm in +X.  
   • Dimensions: x-size = 10 mm (thickness), y-size = 140 mm, z-size = 140 mm.  
   • Base-point: (0, 0, 0).  
   → It intersects the first plate along the common volume 0 ≤ x ≤ 10, 0 ≤ y ≤ 140, 0 ≤ z ≤ 10, giving a rigid 90° corner.

4. No further geometry is required; all parts are connected and meet the 10 mm thickness requirement.

Arrays to be passed to functions.block (in the order plate 1 / cut-out / plate 2):

x_size:        [140, 45, 10]  
y_size:        [140, 45, 140]  
z_size:        [ 10, 10, 140]  
x (base-pt):   [  0, 47.5, 0]  
y (base-pt):   [  0, 47.5, 0]  
z (base-pt):   [  0,   0,  0]  
subtraction:   [False, True, False]

When you ask me to proceed, I will prepare this single functions.block call (followed by functions.finished) but will not execute them until explicitly told.
